answer: A hollow claim of identity is worthless without something scarce behind it: require every agent to hold a unique, randomly assigned data shard, proven by proof-of-replication. A verifier picks a random shard and demands a spot proof within seconds, like standing on a narrow ledge with no room to fake footing. One disk cannot serve two identities at once, because simultaneous challenges for different shards expose the copy. A Sybil grove of fake agents collapses: each extra identity costs a full extra shard of real storage, so scaling fakes scales cost linearly instead of for free.
